logline_en: A timestamp-driven micro-story of the '5 more minutes' snooze spiral whose last frame is its first frame, so the video loops seamlessly.

evidence.claim: Third-party roundup reports a 'vlog timestamps' format trending on Reels in late Oct 2026.
Guides claim rewatch loops matter more than raw length; 20-40 s cited as common for viral Shorts.
Guide claims DM shares/saves weigh more than likes on Reels.

hypotheses: H1: Ending on the exact opening frame (07:00) raises average-view-percentage above our account median (replay signal).
H2: A universally relatable failure (snooze spiral) earns a share rate above our account median because viewers send it to a specific person.
H3: A large on-screen timestamp from frame 0 keeps more viewers past 3 s than a text-question opening (test against concept c_20261031_sound_quiz).
why_now: PROVISIONAL: no platform-measured candidates could be collected in this session (YouTube key missing, Instagram/Apify hosts blocked); evidence below is secondary and unverified. Re-rank against measured clusters before production spend. Timestamp-led storytelling is reported as a current Reels format and needs no trending audio licence.
creative_principle: Use time as the narrative engine: each beat is a visible clock jump, tension rises with the size of the jump, and the punchline resets the clock so the end is the beginning.
originality_notes: No source video was viewed or copied; the format reference is a third-party text description only. Story, script, graphics, synthesized music and TTS narration are produced from scratch by us.
format: kinetic typography + clock graphics, voice-over narration, burned-in captions, seamless loop

edit_plan: Cut on every clock change (~2.4 s average shot, accelerating toward the 07:52 reveal). Scene 10 reuses scene 1's exact layout so the platform's auto-replay looks continuous.
audio_plan: Synthesized pad + 112 BPM pulse at -24 dB under VO; SFX ticks, hit and whoosh generated in FFmpeg; master normalised to -14 LUFS, true peak ≤ -1.5 dBFS. Placeholder espeak-ng voice; replace with a licensed natural Korean TTS or a human read before publishing.
